title: On-Device AI Against Scams: Google DeepMind & MDDI
gist: Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore fine-tuned Google's lightweight Gemma model into a privacy-preserving, on-device scam-detection system that uses a two-stage pipeline to warn users in real time without server-side message scanning.

insights.claim: Scams such as investment fraud, fake job offers and official impersonation make up over half of Singapore's reported crimes and account for more than S$4 billion in losses since 2019.
insights.speaker: JJ Geewax and Miguel de Andrés
insights.so_what: Quantifies the demand for scam-prevention tech in a high-digital-adoption market.

insights.claim: Scam tactics have shifted from simple phishing to complex social engineering through convincing conversations, and such scams now account for up to 80% of all losses.
insights.speaker: JJ Geewax and Miguel de Andrés
insights.so_what: Detection needs to analyse conversation context, not just links or keywords.

insights.claim: The model processes conversations directly on the user's device rather than via cloud scanning, so neither the Singapore Government nor Google can access users' conversations, and it accesses chats only with user consent.
insights.speaker: JJ Geewax and Miguel de Andrés
insights.so_what: A template for safety tooling compatible with end-to-end encryption; edge inference is a growing AI deployment mode.
insights.locator: On-device AI protection without compromising privacy

insights.claim: Google's lightweight Gemma model was fine-tuned on local scam conversations because generic models struggle with local deception techniques such as impersonation of local institutions, banks and figures.
insights.speaker: JJ Geewax and Miguel de Andrés
insights.so_what: Localized fine-tuning of small models can beat generic ones on regional threat types.
insights.locator: On-device AI protection without compromising privacy

insights.claim: A two-stage pipeline manages battery cost: a lightweight classifier screens inbound messages at minimal power, and a fine-tuned Gemma model then analyses a larger conversation snapshot to confirm a threat or discard a false alarm.
insights.speaker: JJ Geewax and Miguel de Andrés
insights.so_what: Cascade design is the practical pattern for running heavy classifiers on phones.
insights.locator: Under the hood: local context and edge efficiency

insights.claim: Development used a sovereign sandbox in GovTech's managed GCP environment, trained only on anonymised scam-report and intelligence data without private or personally identifiable information, and was stress-tested on synthetic dialogues.
insights.speaker: JJ Geewax and Miguel de Andrés
insights.so_what: Government-model-provider partnerships with sovereign cloud isolation are becoming a repeatable pattern.

insights.claim: The rollout will be carefully phased through partnership with the Singapore Government, and DeepMind says it is exploring similar deployments in other countries under its National AI Partnership programme.
insights.speaker: JJ Geewax and Miguel de Andrés
insights.so_what: Possible expansion of government-AI partnerships and national scam-prevention deployments.

source_meta.author: JJ Geewax and Miguel de Andrés
